fields.features_heading: The Case History, Collected Before the Visit
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds a speech therapy intake form around the case history: the concern, when it began, hearing, and home languages.
fields.feature_1:
A concern list in plain words

Offer the concerns a speech clinic sees as choices: speech sounds, stuttering, understanding words, voice, and swallowing. Add one open box for the family to describe it.
fields.feature_2:
Questions worded for whoever answers

Ask who is completing the form first. A parent answering for a child, a spouse answering for an adult, and an adult answering alone each see questions written for them.
fields.feature_3:
Milestones asked as ages, not essays

For a child, ask the age of first words and of first two-word phrases as numbers. The therapist reads two clean values on the record instead of a paragraph of memories.
fields.feature_4:
Hearing and languages side by side

Ask for the date and result of the last hearing test, then the languages used at home, with the main one marked. Both answers sit side by side on the record the therapist opens.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts that carry no answers

When a family submits, the therapist gets an email or Slack alert with a link to the record. The answers stay in the app, saved to a database you own, never in the message.
fields.feature_6:
Your code, in your own repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host the form on the clinic's own site. A developer can add the screens the front desk asks for next year.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Speech Clinics Use the Intake
fields.tab_content_1:
Anabel takes every child who hears Spanish most

Copperbeck Speech and Language asks what languages a family uses at home and which one the child hears most. Yaretzi Solorzano answers Spanish and English for her son Teo, 3, with Spanish heard most. Any child who hears Spanish most is booked with Anabel Arrebola, the clinic's Spanish-speaking therapist.
fields.tab_content_2:
His spouse fills it in, and Ludo is told it is ready

Thornhaven Adult Speech Therapy opens its intake by asking who is completing the form. Edwina Faircloth picks spouse for her husband, Edmund, adds a scheduling phone, and uploads his hospital discharge papers. When she sends it, therapist Ludo Vrettos gets an email that a new intake is ready, with no answers in it.
fields.tab_content_3:
No adult can sit in, so Hana comes to the clinic

Larchgate Speech Therapy offers sessions by video. The intake asks for the device, a quiet room, and, for a child under 8, whether an adult can sit in. Aiko Tsukahara books Hana, 6, on a tablet, but no adult is home on weekday afternoons. Front desk lead Jory Rountree gets the intake and books Hana in the clinic.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 14 waiting families, 3 fit the Tuesday opening

Saddlebrook Speech Clinic has 14 families on its waitlist, and each intake asks which weekday afternoons the child is free. When the Tuesday 4:00 pm slot opens, the app lists the 3 families free then, oldest intake first. Lisette Sauvageau calls the Kovacevic family, waiting since Aug 4, first.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Speech Therapy Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a speech therapy intake form around the first evaluation, then build it with Emergent and send it to new families.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Swap clinical terms for plain questions
fields.howto_step_1_des: Sit with the therapists and write down what they ask in the first ten minutes of an evaluation, such as when the concern began and any past therapy. Each question on the form should trace back to that list. Anything nobody reads before the visit comes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask who the therapy is for before anything else. A child's path covers milestones and school, while an adult's path covers what changed and any recent hospital stay. Neither group scrolls past questions written for the other, and each path stays shorter.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write "Does your child repeat sounds or get stuck on words?" instead of naming the diagnosis you suspect. Offer short choices where they fit, and test each question on someone outside the clinic before it goes in.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a question about the weekdays and times the client can attend, plus whether video sessions work at home. The front desk then books the evaluation from the intake itself, without a round of calls to find a time.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the questions, both paths, and the alert rules into one prompt. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the screen the front desk works from. Ask for changes in plain English, such as a new question for adults.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it as three different families
fields.howto_step_6_des: Fill it in as a parent of a 4-year-old, as an adult client, and as a spouse answering for one. Check that each path shows only its own questions and that every alert reaches the person it names, with no answers inside.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the first ten real intakes
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once the link is live, open the first 10 submissions with a therapist. Look for questions families skipped, misread, or answered the same way every time, and rewrite or cut them. Keep the form only as long as the evaluation needs.

faq_plan.q: What is a speech therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: A speech therapy intake form is the case history a speech clinic collects from a client or family. It records the main concern, when it began, hearing history, and the languages used at home, plus early milestones for a child. Speech-language pathologists treat speech, language, and swallowing disorders in children and adults, and the form leaves room for each.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a speech therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: Write down what your therapists ask at a first evaluation, split it into child and adult paths, and decide who hears about each new intake. Describe all of it to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. It builds the form, the database that stores each case history, and a booking view for the front desk.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a speech therapy intake form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with the main concern and when it began, then hearing history, the languages used at home, and any past therapy or evaluations. For a child, add early milestones and how school is going. For an adult, ask what changed and about any recent hospital stay. Close with insurance and the times the client can attend.

faq_plan.q: Should a speech therapy intake form cover counseling clients too?
faq_plan.a: No. Keep it on communication and swallowing, and give counseling clients their own therapy intake form. The two can share one contact and insurance section. A family that books both then types its details in once.

faq_plan.q: Should a speech therapy intake form ask about hearing?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Ask when the last hearing test was and what it found, and whether the client wears hearing aids. The American Speech-Language-Hearing Association lists hearing as part of communication, alongside speech and language. Put the answer near the top of the record, where the therapist reads it before the evaluation.

faq_plan.q: How should a speech therapy intake form ask about languages at home?
faq_plan.a: Ask which languages each adult at home uses with the client, then which one the client hears most and which one they speak most. Offer a list with an other option rather than a blank box. Show the answers on the booking screen. The front desk can then book a therapist who speaks the language heard most.

faq_plan.q: Can families fill out a speech therapy intake form on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The form is a web page that opens from a link in a text or email. Emergent can build it to show one question per screen, which keeps a long case history manageable on a small display. The same layout suits other clinic forms, such as an acupuncture intake form.

faq_plan.q: Can parents upload past evaluation reports with a speech therapy intake form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an upload field for earlier speech evaluations, a school plan, or a doctor's referral, and each file is saved with the intake record. Make it optional, since a family new to therapy has nothing to send yet.

faq_plan.q: How far ahead of the evaluation should a speech therapy intake form go out?
faq_plan.a: Send the link when the evaluation is booked and ask for it back two days before. That leaves the therapist time to read the case history and the front desk time to check insurance. Set a reminder for any family that has not finished by then.

faq_plan.q: What happens to speech therapy intake form answers after a family submits them?
faq_plan.a: Each submission becomes a record in a database the clinic owns, filed under the client's name. The therapist reads it there before the evaluation, and the front desk books from the same record. With no response caps on an intake form built with Emergent, a busy month never closes it.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3, MSV 20); the query wants a usable speech therapy intake form. The ranking pages for clinic intake forms are clinic PDFs and case history packets. This page names what a speech-language case history collects (the concern, when it started, hearing, home languages, early milestones for children) and shows the form working online in four speech clinics: a bilingual family booked with a Spanish-speaking therapist, a spouse completing the intake for an adult, a teletherapy family sent to the clinic when no adult can sit in, and a waitlist that offers an opening to the longest wait. Alerts only say an intake is ready; answers stay in the app. No clinical, legal or billing advice.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Speech Therapy Intake Form for Every Age and Language'; hero 'Build a speech therapy intake form that splits child and adult questions and saves each case history to a database you own.' (under 130, primary, leads with Build).

intent.evidence: Searcher wants the form and its questions: FAQ 3 'Start with the main concern and when it began, then hearing history, the languages used at home...'; features list concern choices, milestones, hearing, languages; 7-step how-to specific to SLP evaluations.

specificity.evidence: SLP vocabulary throughout: 'age of first words and of first two-word phrases', 'date and result of the last hearing test', 'Does your child repeat sounds or get stuck on words?', Tuesday 4:00 pm waitlist slot.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Copperbeck Speech and Language asks what languages...', 'Ask who is completing the form first.', 'Sit with the therapists and write down...'

craft.evidence: One ', so' ending (tab_content_3 H3), under the limit; list density recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: 'The answers stay in the app, saved to a database you own, never in the message.' Calm, product-led, no AI tells.

truth.evidence: FAQ 1 'treat speech, language, and swallowing disorders in children and adults' and FAQ 5 'lists hearing as part of communication' match the ASHA quoted spans in domain_sources. Emergent claims map to claims_used (alerts, conversational, no-caps, code-export). Health-in-transit clean: feature_5 and tab 2 alerts carry no answers ('with no answers in it'); tab 3 card to Jory Rountree carries only 'No adult can sit in'. Tab 4: 14 waiting, 3 free, Kovacevic since Aug 4 agree with the image.

distinct.evidence: Speech-specific stories (bilingual matching, spouse completing for an adult, teletherapy adult sit-in, waitlist slot); sibling 'therapy intake form' appears only as a FAQ link target, never a heading; QC D2 clean.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first ('Yes. Ask when the last hearing test was...', 'No. Keep it on communication and swallowing...'); hub link in item 2; no brand or file format in questions.
